title: Personality traits shape emotion regulation strategies in children with developmental language disorder
abstract: Abstract Children with Developmental Language Disorder (DLD) often face socio‐emotional challenges beyond language needs, yet the role of personality traits in shaping their emotion regulation (ER) remains underexplored. This study compared ER strategies between children with DLD and typically developing (TD) peers, examined personality predictors of ER and explored the associations between these ER strategies and psychosocial adjustment. Sixty‐eight children (DLD = 27; TD = 41), aged 8–12 years, completed self‐report measures of personality, ER strategies, including Cognitive Reappraisal (CR) and Expressive Suppression (ES), and psychosocial adjustment. Children with DLD reported higher ES use, whereas no group differences emerged for CR. In the DLD group, higher Extraversion predicted greater use of both CR and ES, Neuroticism predicted lower CR and Agreeableness predicted lower ES. Regarding adjustment, higher ES predicted poorer psychosocial adjustment across both groups. Findings highlight personality influences on ER in children with DLD, with implications for socio‐emotional assessment.
